protocols.clinicalDefinitionEn: Safety-first assessment of a new or sudden focal neurologic deficit in a child or adult. This protocol does not diagnose stroke or a stroke mimic; emergency assessment is required. Adult patient. Female.

initialAssessmentQuestions.promptTextEn: What is the exact symptom-onset time and the last-known-well time? If symptoms were noticed on waking, when was the person last known normal before sleep?

Check for sudden face droop, one-sided arm or leg weakness or numbness, speech or understanding difficulty, new loss or double vision, severe dizziness, loss of balance or coordination, inability to walk, or a sudden severe headache.
Is the person difficult to wake, not breathing normally, or having a seizure now?
For a child, record age and any seizure, recent head injury, fever, possible ingestion, or known neurologic condition. These details must not delay the emergency call.
Does the person have diabetes, and is a glucose reading immediately available? Checking glucose must not delay calling 999.

questions.questionTextEn: Is there any sudden face droop, one-sided arm or leg weakness or numbness, abnormal speech or understanding, new loss or double vision, severe dizziness, loss of balance or coordination, inability to walk, sudden severe headache, reduced consciousness, or seizure - including in a child and even if the symptoms improved or stopped?
questions.rationaleEn: FAST signs and sudden vision, balance, coordination, walking, or severe-headache symptoms can indicate stroke. Hypoglycaemia, seizure, migraine, head injury, infection, and other conditions may mimic stroke, particularly in children, but telephone triage cannot safely distinguish them and must not delay emergency assessment.

careAdvice.instructionTextEn: Call Qatar 999 for an ambulance now. Record the exact onset and last-known-well times, including the time last known normal before sleep for wake-up symptoms. Keep the person safe and at rest; do not allow self-driving and do not give food, drink, or medicines because swallowing may be unsafe. If unconscious but breathing normally, place in the recovery position if safe; if not breathing normally, follow the 999 call-handler's resuscitation instructions. A glucose check or possible alternative diagnosis must not delay the call. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care. Call Back If: symptoms worsen; loss of consciousness.

initialAssessmentQuestions.promptTextEn: Where is the rash?
How long ago was the plant contact?
Any blistering or oozing?

What is the exact age; is the patient pregnant; are eyes, mouth, face or genitals involved; and are there breathing symptoms, fever, severe pain, widespread blistering, immune suppression, uncertain plant/chemical exposure or safeguarding concerns?

questions.questionTextEn: Is there sudden swelling of the lips, mouth, throat, or tongue, or difficulty breathing along with the rash?
questions.rationaleEn: Universal emergency rule-out added ahead of the contact dermatitis guidance itself - severe allergic swelling or breathing difficulty requires immediate care, distinct from typical contact dermatitis.

questions.questionTextEn: Are symptoms persistent, recurrent, or severe, or has the triggering substance not responded to treatment?
questions.rationaleEn: NHS.UK guidance: arrange a primary-care review for persistent, recurrent, or severe contact dermatitis symptoms.

questions.questionTextEn: Is this a mild, typical case with none of the features above?
questions.rationaleEn: NHS.UK guidance: a pharmacist can recommend emollients (moisturisers) for mild contact dermatitis.

Call Back If: breathing worsens; swelling spreads or consciousness reduces.

Arrange in-person primary-care review through the Qatar pathway approved for UAT to confirm the cause and assess whether dermatology input is needed. Call Back If: symptoms worsen; not improving with treatment.

Avoid further exposure, gently wash exposed skin and contaminated clothing, and arrange clinician/pharmacist review before creams or medicines are selected. Do not burn suspected plants because smoke exposure may be hazardous. Call Back If: rash worsens, spreads, blisters or becomes infected; eye, mouth, breathing or systemic symptoms.

For an animal exposure, what animal was involved, where did it occur, was skin broken or saliva introduced, and is the animal available for official assessment? Do not try to capture it.

protocols.clinicalDefinitionEn: Safety-first assessment of a penetrating or puncture wound, including an embedded object, bite, needle or high-pressure injection injury, with anatomy, neurovascular status, age, and pregnancy considered. Child patient. Male.

initialAssessmentQuestions.promptTextEn: What caused the wound, when did it happen, and was it a bite, used needle, injection injury, high-pressure tool, dirty object, or intentional injury?
Where is the wound, how deep may it be, and is any object or debris still embedded?
Is bleeding controlled, and beyond the wound is the limb warm and normally coloured with normal feeling, movement, and pulse if trained to check?
Does the wound involve the eye, head, neck, chest, abdomen, groin, genitals, hand, foot, or a joint?
Record age, pregnancy, immune problems, diabetes, medicines affecting bleeding, tetanus vaccination history, and any increasing pain, redness, swelling, pus, fever, or illness.
For an animal exposure, what animal was involved, where did it occur, was skin broken or saliva introduced, and is the animal available for official assessment? Do not try to capture it.
If the patient is under 18, can they speak privately now, is the accompanying caregiver considered safe, and is there an approved safe callback method if contact is lost?
What has a safe parent or caregiver observed about alertness, breathing, pain, swelling, fever, eating or drinking, sleep, play, and normal activity?
